subject: reporting results in a journal paper

messages.author: 58c9b920899044d5
messages.subject: reporting results in a journal paper
parts:
Hi all, 

I am currently writing a paper with my SEM results but not really sure what would be a good standard of reporting results.

My model is a bit complex - it has 6 exogenous variables, two mediators and ten endogenous variables (and several control variables). the 6 exogenous variables are all single item with binary option. Mediators are latent variables from a standardised scale. As for the endogenous variables, it mixes latent variables (standardised scales too) and single item binary variables. 

I found many papers having two-step SEM: step 1 is CFA for the measurement model (most of them put all the measurements in one model and run a CFA) and step 2 is for the structural model (mediation). I was wondering if this is necessary? If yes, also given that my model has some single item measures, should they be included in the measurement model?

Also, I found that two of the measurements showed poor composition reliability and some items have low factor loading (between 0.1-0.4). Can I still include them in the model?

BW,
Alison
